headline: Net loss narrows year-over-year as one-time pay charge fades
summary_short: Net loss narrowed 61.9% y/y to $215.7 million (diluted EPS -$0.28) as R&D and G&A expenses fell sharply against a stock-compensation-heavy year-ago quarter, while cash and short-term investments totaled $690.7 million.
summary_long: Total operating expenses fell 61.2% y/y to $220.5 million, driven almost entirely by a combined $410.1 million drop in stock-based compensation after Summit modified its performance-based option awards in Q2 2025 — not by underlying cost discipline. Clinical trial expense rose $36.9 million y/y on HARMONi-3, HARMONi-7 and HARMONi-GI3 enrollment. Sequentially, net loss widened from $189.4 million to $215.7 million as trial spending ramped. Summit remains pre-revenue with no approved product. Cash and short-term investments totaled $690.7 million after a $227.4 million raise under its equity Distribution Agreement, but the filing states these balances are not sufficient to fund planned operations for at least one year, reiterating going-concern doubt.
